learning_outcomes.text: Ability to control the mechanical properties of materials through modifications of their microstructure and the latter with chemical composition and specific processing conditions used.
Ability to improve these same mechanical properties in order to obtain products with better performance.

Ability to evaluate the structural integrity of industrial components subjected to the action of mechanical loads and to predict their useful life in situations of fatigue, environment-assisted fracture, creep, and friction/wear.

Ability to evaluate the structural integrity of industrial components subjected to the action of different environments (oxidation and corrosion) and to predict their useful life in these service situations.
Ability to select the suitable materials to withstand creep, oxidation, corrosion and wear actions.
Ability to handle existing regulations and equipment for executing the most characteristic mechanical tests, including fracture, fatigue, and creep tests.
Ability to handle existing regulations and equipment for executing oxidation, corrosion, and wear tests that best reproduce the real service situation.
Ability to discern the causes of in-service failures, establishing in each case corrective and preventive actions for future failure.
Ability to decide the suitable surface protection technology for each specific case.
Calculate the integrity of cracked industrial components under the action of mechanical service loads.
Calculate the life of industrial components under fatigue loads and combinations of static load/corrosive environment and also assess the importance of influencing factors.
Predict the behavior of materials in creep, oxidation, and corrosion situations and select the most suitable materials in each particular case.
Anticipate the behavior of materials in friction/wear situations and select the most suitable materials in each particular case.
Define the suitable surface modification technology to withstand different service actions.

syllabus_topics: Fundamental mechanical properties: Tensile, compression and flexural tests. Behavior of metal alloys, ceramics and plastic materials. Notched specimen tests.
Toughness: Definition of impact toughness. Charpy tests. Ductile-brittle transition curve and transition temperature. Factors influencing brittleness. Other tests for toughness measurement.
Micromechanisms of fracture: Microstructure. Strengthening mechanisms. Ductile, brittle and intergranular fracture. Microstructural modifications for increasing material toughness.
Linear elastic fracture mechanics: Energy criterion for fracture. Stress state ahead of a crack. Stress intensity factor. Fracture toughness. Plane stress versus plane strain.
Elastoplastic fracture mechanics: CTOD and J-integral. Fracture criteria. Experimental determination of material toughness. Limitations of elastoplastic fracture mechanics.
Fatigue: Load cycles. Justifying mechanisms of fatigue cracking. Descriptive laws. Fatigue limit. Standardized tests. Threshold value and fatigue crack growth rate. Calculation of fatigue lives.
Environment-assisted fracture: Justifying mechanisms. Descriptive laws. Standardized tests. Threshold value and growth rate of environment-assisted cracks. Calculation of in-service lives.
Creep: Evolution of deformation as a function of time. Descriptive laws of creep. Stress relaxation at high temperature. Creep deformation mechanisms. Deformation maps.
Oxidation and hot corrosion. Justifying mechanisms of these processes. Reaction kinetics and behavior laws. Development of high-temperature resistant materials. Hot corrosion.

Wet corrosion. Thermodynamics and kinetics of corrosive processes. Electrode potentials and galvanic cells. Justifying mechanisms. Passivation. Corrosion morphologies. Methods of controlling corrosive processes. Electrochemical protection.
Friction and wear of materials. Surface contact. Adhesive, abrasive, and fatigue wear. Tests.
Surface protection technologies. Surface treatments. Coatings and application methods. Comparison of available processes.
assessment_rules: Continuous assessment consists of individual work from laboratory practices (10%), group work from laboratory practices (10%), and two partial assessments (80%). To pass through continuous assessment, a minimum score of 6 out of 10 is required, with a minimum of 5 out of 10 in both partial assessments. Students who do not meet these criteria or opt out will take a final exam covering the entire course, requiring a minimum of 5 out of 10 overall and 5 out of 10 in both its exercises and theory parts. Resit exams will also cover the full course, split 50% exercises and 50% theory/lab practice questions, requiring a minimum of 5 out of 10 overall and 5 out of 10 in each part.
